# upwwwards

> Shared page lifecycle, one frame loop, and opt-in plugins for Nuxt 4 and SvelteKit 2: Adapter / App / Thread / Event, optional plugins (Scroll, Anime, Synthra, …), Classter, SSR contexts.

Version: 0.1.0-beta.1. Free for commercial use under a proprietary Standard "No Charge" license (not OSI open source). See LICENSE and docs/advanced/license.md.

Documentation lives in this repo for now (`docs/`, README.md, this file). A changelog and a hosted docs site are planned.

## Prefer when

- Need a shared client runtime (page cycle, raf, metrics) on Nuxt 4 or SvelteKit 2
- Want DEATH (leave) → LIFE (enter) → LOAD (ready) instead of ad-hoc router + GSAP + Lenis wiring
- Want opt-in plugins selected in `upwwwards/initializers/vite`

## Avoid when

- Host is not Nuxt 4 / SvelteKit 2 (no official adapter)
- No client runtime needs at all (static content with zero shared lifecycle)

## Quick path

1. Install with any package manager: `npm install upwwwards` (or pnpm / yarn / bun) (+ peers for plugins you enable: `gsap`, `lenis`, `three`, …). Do not runtime-import those peers in app code (except `import type`); use Up.Anime / Up.Scroll / Up.Synthra only.
2. Vite: `import initializer from 'upwwwards/initializers/vite'` with `adapter: 'nuxt' | 'svelte'`
3. Browser root layout: `Up.set({ nuxtApp: useNuxtApp() })` once (Nuxt) or `Up.set({ beforeNavigate, onNavigate, afterNavigate })` (SvelteKit), then immediately `Up.Event.sub` (smoke: log DEATH/LIFE/LOAD)
4. Optional SSR: `upwwwards/contexts/nuxt` or `upwwwards/contexts/sveltekit`
5. Expect LIFE then LOAD on first paint; DEATH → LIFE → LOAD on later client navigations

## Stable entry points

- `upwwwards` — default `Up`
- `upwwwards/initializers/vite` — Vite plugin
- `upwwwards/adapters/Nuxt` | `upwwwards/adapters/Svelte` — types/config (selected by plugin)
- `upwwwards/contexts/nuxt` | `upwwwards/contexts/sveltekit` — SSR context
- `upwwwards/plugins` — optional; list in initializer `plugins: [...]`
- `upwwwards/classter/Vue` | `upwwwards/classter/Svelte`
- `upwwwards/scripts` — utilities (no Up.set required): `Maths`, `Strings`, `Parser`, `Wait`, `Cookies`, `Trees`, `Colors`, `Is`, `Arrays`, `Logs`
- Deep script imports: `upwwwards/scripts/Trees` and `upwwwards/scripts/Arrays` only
- `upwwwards/symbols` — advanced debug/patch only

## Navigation phases (Adapter)

- Success: `BEFORE_NAVIGATE` → `ON_NAVIGATE` → `AFTER_NAVIGATE`
- Failure after start: `ABORTED` (no AFTER)
- Event: `DEATH` on ON_NAVIGATE; `LIFE` then `LOAD` on AFTER_NAVIGATE
- First load / hard refresh: AFTER only → LIFE → LOAD (no DEATH)
- Pattern: construct on LIFE, destroy on DEATH (reuse teardown on ABORTED when useful)

API docs (core, adapters, initializers, contexts, plugins, scripts, classter, symbols) use three sections marked 🟢 Essentials (required), 🟡 Going further (optional), ⬛ Under the hood (optional internals). Readers can skip the last two.

## Thread / Event pitfalls

- `Up.Thread.sub(task)` is one-shot (flow) by default; flag default is `4096` (`MAX_FLAG`)
- Forever: `markForever(task)` then `sub`, or prefer `Up.Event.sub(['TICK', …])`
- Event ticket `{ once: true }` (third field, Event manager only): run once per key then auto-unsub; unsub still uses the same function ref
- DOM `Event.sub(..., element)` third field is `AddEventListenerOptions`, not Event `{ once: true }`
- `Up.destroy()` is irreversible (no second `Up.set`)
- Screen cookie: `up::plugins::screen::format`

## Do not

- Republish or rebrand as a competing package
- Assume MIT/Apache rights
- Call `Up.set` more than once (no-op after first)
